C1.text: Every message, both directions, is exactly **one JSON object per line**, UTF-8, terminated by `\n`. No length prefixes, no concatenated JSON, no blank lines (the mirror never emits them; a read that returns an empty line is EOF).

C2.text: Clients **MUST** enforce the uniform **65,535-byte payload** limit (not counting the terminating newline) on raw UTF-8 bytes before JSON parsing and after final encoding. They **MUST NOT** emit a larger line or use an unbounded receive accumulator. Keep individual messages small. `spec.sources` is the portable source form only when the complete final registration fits this limit; version 1 does not chunk sources or results.

C3.text: All protocol messages are discriminated by the string field `"proto_step"`. Clients **MUST** dispatch on `proto_step` and **MUST** tolerate (ignore) unknown additional fields in mirror messages — the wire contract is field-additive.

C4.text: A replay, validation, trace-generation, or exploration flow **MUST** begin with a `register*` message (`register`, `register_traces`, `register_trace_gen`, `register_validate`, `register_explore*`, or the async variants). Server-mode `query_job`, `await_job`, and `cancel_job` may operate on an existing job ID without a new registration on the querying connection; unknown IDs return `job_status` with phase `unknown`. Stdio rejects async operations with `register_error`. The pure phase-indexed session machine constrains successful transitions; malformed inputs remain representable and are rejected at the shell/codec or protocol boundary.

C5.text: After a terminal mirror message (`all_steps_done`, `gen_traces_done`, `spec_validated` for validate-only, `explorer_session_done`, `step_mismatch`, `register_error`, or `protocol_error`), the flow is over. A client **MUST NOT** send further flow messages on that session; start a new connection instead.

C6.text: A client **SHOULD** close connections cleanly and **MUST** tolerate the server closing first. On connection end the server cancels and evicts exactly that session's async jobs (Haskell `endSession` semantics) — jobs submitted on other connections are unaffected, but a dropped connection loses its own in-flight work.

C7.text: There are no pings, heartbeats, or idle timeouts at the protocol level (the server's 10 s `SO_RCVTIMEO` applies only to the TLS handshake window, not to established sessions). A client that needs liveness **MAY** poll with `query_job` or simply open a probe connection.

C8.text: The client **MUST** answer every `initial_state` and `next_step` with exactly one `report_state`. Staying silent wedges the session (the mirror's read blocks; on the worker-pool server a silent connection parks a pool worker — this is a documented accepted-divergence DoS surface on plain TCP).

C9.text: `report_state.state` **MUST** contain the full observable state as ITF values. The mirror diffs it against the expected trace state with `filterMeta` semantics: keys starting with `#` plus `action_taken` and `parameters` are excluded from comparison. Everything else is compared deeply — extra keys are reported as `extra` hints, missing ones as `missing`.

C10.text: On `step_mismatch` the session ends **without** a trailing `all_steps_done` (spec-faithful; the Haskell server sends one — documented divergence). Clients **MUST** treat `step_mismatch` as terminal. Hints are capped at 50 plus one `truncated` hint, in sorted-key order; see `interface-reference.md` §3.1 for the hint schema.

C11.text: Integers in state **MUST** be encodable as `{"#bigint": "<decimal>"}`. The mirror also *accepts* bare integral JSON numbers on decode (Haskell parity), but a conforming client **SHOULD** always emit `#bigint` — that is what every encoder in the ecosystem produces.

C12.text: Trace length and stride choices are nondeterministic (apalache search order). Clients **MUST NOT** hardcode expected step counts; drive the loop until a terminal message.

C13.text: To keep a client server-filesystem-independent, ship specs inline: `"spec": {"sources": ["---- MODULE M ----\n…", …]}`. The client **MUST** include the full `EXTENDS`/`INSTANCE` closure in `sources`; the server materializes them into a per-session owned temp dir (never the server's cwd — run-dir isolation is gated by `counter_spec`). The complete compact registration **MUST** still fit C2. For a larger closure, use a pre-provisioned server-side `specPath`, an explicit external generation/artifact workflow, or a future versioned transfer protocol.

C14.text: `ApalacheConfig` optional fields follow Haskell `.:?` semantics: absent ≡ explicit `null`. Defaults on decode: `invariant` and `paramVars` `""`, `lengthBound` 10, the rest `null`. A client **MAY** omit optional keys (JS clients do) or send explicit nulls (Haskell clients do); both are conforming.

C15.text: Specs declaring `CONSTANTS` **MUST** set `constInit`. `paramVars` names a spec variable lifted out of state comparison into step parameters (see `tools/CounterSpec.lean` for the resulting `{"parameters":{"parameters":{"stride":N}}}` shape after resplit).

C16.text: `register_validate`/`register_validate_async` take `bound` ∈ [1, 100]; out-of-range bounds are rejected synchronously at registration before any state change.

C17.text: `jobId`s are process-unique and **cross-connection visible**: any connection may query/await/cancel any live job. Clients **MAY** submit on one connection and await on another, but note C6: the submitter's disconnect cancels and evicts its jobs regardless of who is awaiting.

C18.text: `await_job` **MUST** be treated as long-polling: without `timeoutSecs` it blocks until the job terminates; with it, a timeout returns `job_status` (non-terminal), never an error. Terminal results are idempotent — re-awaiting a finished job returns the same `job_result` until eviction.

C19.text: Cancellation is cooperative but lethal to the apalache child: `cancel_job` on a running job terminates the spawned `apalache-mc` process. A client **SHOULD** cancel jobs it no longer needs rather than dropping the connection (which cancels anyway, per C6).

C20.text: A completed validate job's `outcome.validate` payload is **identical** to what the synchronous `register_validate` flow would have answered for the same config (machine-proven congruence, `async-enablement-design.md` §6.4) — clients **MAY** share result handling between sync and async paths.

C21.text: `job_status.phase` `"unknown"` is answered exactly for never-submitted or evicted ids. Clients **MUST NOT** retry-loop on `unknown` expecting the job to appear.

C22.text: A client **SHOULD** size its own connection pool ≤ the server's `--jobs` when driving sustained load (the 300-cycle stress harness uses exactly 4 against `--jobs 4`). Oversubscribing connections is legal — excess connections queue at the accept backlog — but oversubmitted *jobs* are rejected at submit with `register_error` ("job queue full"), and clients **MUST** handle that reply.

C23.text: Clients **MUST NOT** assume any ordering between jobs submitted on different connections.

C24.text: TLS 1.3 only; the client **MUST** present a certificate chaining to the server's CA (`--ca`). No client certificate → handshake failure (server logs `tls: handshake rejected` 1:1).

C25.text: Server identity is verified by **SAN only** (hostname or IP-literal SAN; CN is ignored). Clients **MUST** connect using a name present in the server cert's SAN — e.g. the production cert carries `IP:192.168.150.219` only, so a loopback `127.0.0.1` connect fails verification even though it is the same machine.

C26.text: Fingerprint pinning: when the deployment pins (registry discovery, `--pin`), the client **MUST** verify the server's SHA-256 certificate fingerprint (case-insensitive compare). A wrong pin **MUST** fail the connection before any protocol bytes flow.

C27.text: Client key files **MUST** be `0600` on POSIX (enforced; Windows ACLs govern there). Wildcard server certificates match the leftmost label only (OpenSSL semantics — stricter than the Haskell `tls` package; accepted divergence, fail-closed).

MI1.text: Existing non-negotiated entry points **MUST** remain source-compatible, send no `modelInterface` field, and retain their existing replay behavior. The extension is allowed only on `register` and `register_traces`; version 1 does not extend validate, trace-generation, async-job, or explorer registrations.

MI2.text: A client **MUST** treat a descriptor and generated metadata as inert interface data. It **MUST NOT** evaluate or compile received content, load a module/plugin/symbol named by it, retrieve an executable adapter, or expose expected trace state to the application adapter.

MI3.text: A compiled client **MUST** embed the compiler-produced semantic digest and normalized contract, select a precompiled binding, and perform no runtime descriptor interpretation, code generation, dynamic loading, or artifact retrieval. Generated files **MUST NOT** be hand-edited.

MI4.text: The build and runtime configurations **MUST** agree on the effective `paramVars` value and the selected local computer contract (`mirrors.state-computer/v1`, or the optional async contract in section 9.7). A configuration mismatch is a local failure before any application handler or observer runs.

MI5.text: The outer protocol stays field-additive, but every versioned negotiation, failure, companion-contract, and descriptor object **MUST** use strict duplicate-aware decoding: reject duplicate keys, unknown fields, invalid field combinations, noncanonical digests, and resource-limit violations. Optional fields accept absent or explicit `null`; encoders omit absent values.

MI6.text: A client **MUST** send the complete generated `ContractV1` inline. The reserved contract-digest reference is unsupported in version 1, and the client **MUST NOT** infer a companion file from the server-side `specPath`.

MI7.text: The contract and expected digest **MUST** come from the same verified generated metadata. The client **MUST NOT** substitute a model name, `interfaceVersion`, provenance digest, version range, or “compatible” digest for exact semantic identity.

MI8.text: Under `require`, a missing reply, required failure, malformed reply, unsupported schema, unexpected status, or digest mismatch **MUST** close the flow before any adapter factory, SUT constructor, action, observer, or other application callback runs. No `report_state` may be sent.

MI9.text: A `verify` client **MUST** accept normal negotiated replay only from a strictly valid `matched` reply whose descriptor schema is accepted and whose parsed semantic digest exactly equals the embedded digest. It **MUST** reject descriptor bytes on `matched` and any status/field combination not allowed by `model-interface-runtime-distribution-design.md` §9.

MI10.text: `prefer` **MUST NOT** weaken a digest pin. It may continue after an old-server omission or a permitted non-pin failure only when the caller explicitly supplied a separate legacy fallback factory. Libraries **MUST NOT** silently change `require` to `prefer` or reuse the negotiated factory as an implicit fallback.

MI11.text: Registry lookup **MUST** use the exact four-part key and return exactly one factory. It **MUST NOT** guess “latest”, search version ranges, choose the closest digest, or try several adapters until one works.

MI12.text: The selected factory **MUST** run only after successful negotiation (or an explicit permitted legacy fallback), return a fresh binding for that session, and perform no remote artifact retrieval. The runner **MUST** recheck the binding digest and effective configuration before entering replay.

MI13.text: Negotiated and legacy entry points **SHOULD** converge on the same replay loop after binding selection. After construction, the runner **MUST** attempt `dispose` exactly once on success, `step_mismatch`, decode or transport failure, a thrown `StateComputer`, and binding-validation failure. A cleanup failure is secondary to an earlier primary failure.

MI14.text: Client-local negotiation failures **SHOULD** expose stable codes such as `negotiation_missing`, `descriptor_digest_invalid`, `adapter_not_registered`, `adapter_ambiguous`, `binding_digest_mismatch`, `binding_config_mismatch`, `adapter_factory_failed`, and `legacy_fallback_unavailable`. A structured `register_error.modelInterface` code remains a server failure and **MUST NOT** be collapsed into those local codes or into a conformance mismatch.

MI15.text: Before caching or using `resolved`, a descriptor client **MUST** validate its strict schema, exact `descriptorBytes`, structural limits, and canonical semantic digest. It **MUST** enforce the 32,768-byte inline descriptor limit and the 65,535-byte final line limit; it must never accept a truncated, chunked, compressed, or partially decoded descriptor.

MI16.text: `not_modified` succeeds only when a local cache entry exists and its bytes recompute to the advertised digest under the same byte, depth, and node limits. A missing or corrupt entry aborts the session; retry on a new connection without `ifNoneMatch`.

MI17.text: A dynamic handler registry **MUST** match every stable initializer, action, and observation ID exactly, contain no extras, accept input records keyed by the declared stable input IDs, and declare the same semantic digest as the verified descriptor. It **MUST** support every descriptor type and map aliases only to their primary action. It validates all inputs before mutation, performs exactly one observation pass after an action, and permanently poisons the binding after an invalid observer value. It never constructs handler bodies from descriptor content.

MI18.text: A semantic digest **MUST NOT** be treated as authentication or authorization. Clients retain C24–C27 server authentication, SAN validation, and pinning. An authorization failure is terminal and must cause zero SUT calls; clients **MUST NOT** retry it by silently dropping negotiation.

SO1.text: A client advertising shared sandbox orchestration **MUST** delegate common stage transitions, sandbox admission, artifact handoff, worker lifecycle, cancellation, and cleanup to the shared MirrorGate process implementation. Native facades **MUST NOT** independently reimplement that state machine or embed a second language client's evaluator as an implicit prerequisite.

SO2.text: A client **SHOULD** expose one native evaluation entry point that starts a compatible local orchestration process or connects to an explicitly configured trusted instance. A separate manual daemon-start step **SHOULD NOT** be necessary for local use. The facade **MUST** distinguish process ownership from session ownership: it closes its own sessions and terminates a process only when it owns that process. Sharing an implementation does not require all users or evaluations to share one global daemon.

SO3.text: Implementations **MUST** keep orchestration control, the Mirrors model protocol, and public-port worker RPC distinct. The control channel belongs to trusted callers; it is not an additional worker capability. Existing `GateSession` Python calls and administrative CLI flags are not a versioned cross-language control protocol. Worker `hello/create/invoke` messages **MUST NOT** be repurposed to select host mounts or private specs.

SO4.text: The model-facing generated binding and replay driver **MUST** remain trusted. Only declared initializer/action inputs, actual observations, and permitted lifecycle controls cross the worker boundary. Raw Mirrors messages, `StateComputer`/`ReplayComputer` arguments, expected states, private trace coordinates, specifications, and credentials **MUST NOT** be forwarded to submitted code. Language clients retain their native binding/value conversion; this is not permission to duplicate shared orchestration policy.

SO5.text: Execution-worker launch **MUST** wait for successful required model negotiation and backend admission. This includes native artifact startup, whose loader/pre-main code can run before a shim handshake. The shim **MUST** additionally gate its managed adapter factory on valid `hello/create`. Authoring and build may precede negotiation only under their own restricted profiles; MI8's zero-callback requirement concerns evaluation binding/SUT construction, not separately authorized source preparation.

SO6.text: Source/artifact handoff **MUST** use supervisor-owned snapshots with recorded identities, not a live writable authoring mount in evaluation. Protocol version, public semantic digest, artifact hash, runtime profile, backend policy, and private model revision **MUST** remain separate identities. A worker echoing an interface digest **MUST NOT** be treated as artifact authenticity, caller authorization, or proof of honest observations.

SO7.text: Clients **MUST** preserve separate failures for control compatibility, backend admission, build failure, model negotiation, worker transport/protocol, application failure, timeout/cancellation, and Mirrors `step_mismatch`. Failure to establish requested isolation **MUST NOT** fall back to a raw subprocess. The model-interface `prefer` policy does not authorize a weaker sandbox, public disclosure, or retry of a failed mutation.

SO8.text: The shared process **MUST** be the authority for session resource ownership and bounded forced teardown. Client disposal releases the session's worker handle; it does not create an independent competing cleanup loop. Success, mismatch, partial construction, callback failure, cancellation, disconnect, and timeout **MUST** converge on at-most-once logical release and bounded cleanup. Cooperative cancellation is not proof that code has stopped. Preserve the primary error if cleanup also fails. Closing one session **MUST NOT** terminate resources owned by another session or an attached shared daemon.

SO9.text: A shared control endpoint **MUST** restrict administration to trusted callers and bind handles to the owning session/principal. Submitted artifacts and agent requests **MUST NOT** select or expand host mounts, permissions, credentials, or management access. A remote control transport requires its own authenticated authorization contract; Mirrors mTLS authorization does not automatically authorize MirrorGate control operations.

SO10.text: The agent host **MUST** mediate every access-capable implementation tool and keep private data out of prompts, retrieval, and tool results. Detailed evaluator reports remain trusted unless explicitly released by policy. Ordinary client APIs that return private mismatch diagnostics are not suitable agent-facing tools without this disclosure boundary. Sandboxing **MUST NOT** be advertised as proving observation fidelity or preventing all information inference from permitted inputs and verdicts.

SO11.text: Before advertising support, each facade **MUST** implement the same versioned MirrorGate control contract and shared fixtures. MirrorGate control v1 specifies framing and bounds, version/capability negotiation, request correlation, session/handle ownership, events/results, stable error families, cancellation/disconnect behavior, and cleanup completion. SDKs **MUST NOT** independently invent command sequences or parse human CLI diagnostics as this contract. Backend capability reporting **MUST** distinguish enforced guarantees from unavailable features and per-process/UID limits from aggregate quotas. The existing frozen worker v1 contract remains independently versioned.

SO12.text: A client **MUST** pass common control/lifecycle fixtures and actual backend tests for every advertised profile. At least two language facades **MUST** demonstrate equivalent outcomes through the same orchestration implementation before it is claimed as verified across client languages. Record client language, worker runtime, control version, and backend separately. Existing Node/Rust worker conformance alone does not meet that criterion.

C1.note: Outbound LF terminated UTF-8 JSONL and inbound fatal UTF-8 framing.

C2.note: 65535-byte final outbound payload and bounded raw pending inbound line before parsing; this does not establish a total queued-message memory quota.

C3.note: Dispatch uses proto_step; ordinary message field selection ignores additions.

C4.note: Runners send their registration first; Connection allows job query/await/cancel without a new registration.

C5.note: Literal C5 requires new connection after register_error; section10 says terminal for that attempt. SDK preserves async connection; parent confirms server queue-full preserves it and other SDKs agree. Closing evicts unrelated jobs underC6. Reconcile guide/server semantics before client changes. Aggregate clarification: C5 blanket session termination conflicts with section 10 register-attempt wording and the server async loop. Do not automatically close a connection that may own other jobs.

C6.note: One-shot replay closes transport on all outcomes; framing closure yields terminal receive failure.

C7.note: Optional liveness probe uses query_job for an unknown ID; no protocol heartbeat introduced.

C8.note: One report_state per normally completed initialization/action; callback errors terminate and close.

C9.note: Encoder retains every application-returned observable field including prototype-looking keys; completeness/fidelity depends on adapter.

C10.note: Mismatch throws immediately and does not wait for all_steps_done.

C11.note: Integer values encode as decimal #bigint markers without native-number coercion.

C12.note: Loop terminates on mirror terminal reply rather than configured expected count.

C13.note: Recursive EXTENDS/INSTANCE closure with skipped strings/comments, dependency deduplication and ambiguity rejection; caller must select inline sources.

C14.note: Optional undefined properties omitted; null values retained as permitted by server contract.

C15.note: Caller-supplied ApalacheConfig exposes constInit/paramVars; source resolver does not independently prove a model constants initializer exists.

C16.note: Both sync and async validate reject noninteger/outside1..100 bounds before sending.

C17.note: Public job methods accept external job IDs, with no submitting-connection restriction.

C18.note: await maps job_status to nonterminal result and leaves request timeout absent unless caller chooses one.

C19.note: Explicit cooperative cancel_job sends retained; physical Apalache termination is server responsibility.

C20.note: Async validate payload decoded through same ValidateResult shape; server congruence not re-proven by client.

C21.note: Unknown phase becomes JobEvictedError in handle await and is never internally retried.

C22.note: Queue-full errors are classified explicitly; connection reuse follows server async session implementation, subject to C5/section10 guide ambiguity. Caller owns pooling.

C23.note: Only exchanges within one connection serialize; no cross-connection ordering assumed.

C24.note: TLS1.3-only options, CA bundle and required client certificate/key supplied.

C25.note: X509 checkIP/checkHost with subject never prevents CN fallback; hostname defaults to connection host.

C26.note: DER leaf SHA256 pin verified before returning transport; wrong pin destroys socket.

C27.note: The guide literally requires 0600. This implementation rejects group/other access but permits owner-only 0400/0700 and special-bit variants. This is a policy/wording discrepancy, not demonstrated secret disclosure.

MI1.note: Legacy registrations omit extension; negotiated encoder restricts extension to register/register_traces at model-interface.ts1267.

MI2.note: Received descriptor parsed as inert data; local callback map supplies executable behavior; no received module loading.

MI3.note: Compiled path uses provided generated contract/digest and exact precompiled registry. Generated provenance/freshness remains build gate obligation.

MI4.note: Callback negotiation admits an invalid target/computer pairing. The invalid callback selection is accepted and invokes factory/computer/dispose once. The same pair with execution: "sync" rejects locally with state_computer_contract_mismatch and zero calls/sends.

MI5.note: First reply decoded from bounded duplicate-aware strict raw parser; every versioned object uses exact schema validation; outer additions ignored.

MI6.note: Inline ContractV1 required; reserved digest references explicitly rejected.

MI7.note: Verification request and registry digest derived from same generated metadata; exact digest compared after match.

MI8.note: First-reply strict decode and authorization complete before any deferred binding/registry factory; prebuilt dynamic registry explicitly has weaker zero-construction scope.

MI9.note: matched requires supported descriptor schema, digest and no descriptor bytes; authorizeReply matches expected digest.

MI10.note: Prefer requires separate explicit fallback; mismatch always fatal and structured registration errors throw before fallback.

MI11.note: Immutable registry exact four-key matching; ambiguity rejected, no nearest/latest selection.

MI12.note: Factory after authorized matched/fallback; digest and configuration rechecked before replay. Freshness is factory contract.

MI13.note: Created binding disposed once on success/failure; dynamic returned scope cleanup retained even binding validation fails; earlier primary retained.

MI14.note: Structured server failures have ModelInterfaceRegistrationError distinct from local stable NegotiatedRunnerError codes.

MI15.note: Resolved descriptor canonical bytes/digest checked; strict depth/node/type limits and32768byte descriptor/65535byte line limits.

MI16.note: Cached bytes and digest recomputed; corruption quarantined. not_modified requires sent validator and exact valid cache entry.

MI17.note: Exact registry keys/digest, aliases same action, input projection before mutation, one observer pass, poisoned lifecycle after invalid output.

MI18.note: Unauthorized structured registration fails before SUT; no silent retry without negotiation; authenticated transport constructed separately.

SO1.note: Facade uses control SDK and session reservation; no independent sandbox process state machine.

SO2.note: One-call owned launch and explicit attached Unix endpoint; transport ownership separates process termination authority.

SO3.note: Private attachment/control distinct from worker hello/create/invoke; Mirrors registration retained in trusted ECMA transport.

SO4.note: Native proxy forwards declared stable input IDs/converted values and observation request; no expected states/private coordinates forwarded.

SO5.note: Deferred factory receives matched authority, then session.authorize/acquireWorker; physical native startup confinement requires actual backend test.

SO6.note: Prepared identity preserves source/artifact/manifest/runtime/policy separately; actual immutable snapshot ownership belongs to supervisor.

SO7.note: Failure family separation plus cancellation/deadline public variants; no raw subprocess fallback found.

SO8.note: Worker closes through owner-bound Gate reservation release and awaited cleanup. Real descendant teardown/ownership requires backend verification.

SO9.note: Opaque owner-bound handles, trusted local stdio/Unix endpoints and restrictive socket-path checks; no remote control transport advertised here.

SO10.note: Default redacted public result and trusted diagnostics exist. Complete agent access-capable tool mediation cannot be established from client library alone.

SO11.note: Versioned control framing, capability scope, correlation, ownership and lifecycle validation; v1/v2 additive support independently selected.

SO12.note: Current source audit does not execute common fixtures or real backend/two-facade matrix; earlier ledger scope must not be extended to a current runtime pass.

C1.note: Compact JSON object encoding, LF transport framing and blank-line/EOF handling; stdio/TCP/TLS paths.

C2.note: Raw std::string byte bounds before parsing and final writes, bounded 4096-byte read chunks, identical TLS cap. No fresh runtime qualification.

C3.note: Dispatches on string proto_step; known-message decoder ignores additional outer fields; negotiation is closed separately.

C4.note: All replay/validate/generation/explore runners send registration; async job control permits existing IDs and stdio refuses async before dispatch.

C5.note: Synchronous and exploration runners close on terminal messages. Async register_error intentionally leaves the borrowed transport open. C5 requires a new connection, whereas guide section 10 says terminal for that register attempt; clarify the guide before imposing close-on-queue-full (which evicts existing owned jobs). Aggregate clarification: C5 blanket session termination conflicts with section 10 register-attempt wording and the server async loop. Do not automatically close a connection that may own other jobs.

C6.note: Replay paths close owned flow transport on normal/error outcomes, tolerate server EOF; asynchronous helper transport is caller-owned.

C7.note: No invented heartbeat; raw receive has no established-session timeout, configurable TCP connect and TLS handshake bounds; query helpers available.

C8.note: Shared stepping loop calls StateComputer once and sends exactly one ReportState for initial_state/next_step; exceptions terminate before reporting.

C9.note: SDK State and ITF codecs preserve all ordinary keys; caller supplies truthful full observations. Generated Counter port emits actual count; SDK cannot prove arbitrary application observation fidelity.

C10.note: StepMismatch returns failure and closes immediately without waiting for all_steps_done; expected/actual/hints retained.

C11.note: Native arbitrary-precision integers always encode #bigint; bare integer JSON accepted on decode.

C12.note: Loop is terminal driven and has no fixed step count. preset_client is explicitly supplied user sequence, separate from normal runner.

C13.note: Inline ApalacheSpec sources plus recursive EXTENDS/INSTANCE closure collector, canonical deduplication and explicit missing/ambiguous import errors. Builtin modules are intentionally not vendored.

C14.note: Config encoder omits absent optionals and sends default invariant/paramVars/lengthBound through typed config.

C15.note: constInit and paramVars exposed and encoded exactly. Application selects constInit for its spec; Counter integration sets CInit/parameters.

Aggregate clarification: C5 blanket session termination conflicts with section 10 register-attempt wording and the server async loop. Do not automatically close a connection that may own other jobs.

C6.note: The validate CLI brackets transport with tcpClose/tlsClose and maps EOF/errors to exit 2. Library ownership remains caller-managed. tlsClose sends best-effort bye; underlying socket release is documented at process exit.

C7.note: No protocol heartbeat or idle deadline assumed by the client library; blocking await supports indefinite waits.

C8.note: InitialState/NextStep dispatches the handler, sends exactly one ReportState, then waits for StepOk or mismatch.

C9.note: Application clientHandler returns the full observable Map. Arbitrary observation fidelity remains application responsibility.

C10.note: handleStep returns Left on StepMismatch immediately without waiting for AllStepsDone. Historical Haskell SERVER trailing-done behavior is not a client defect.

C11.note: Unbounded Integer is emitted as #bigint decimal; integral JSON numbers are accepted. Malformed ITF defense was not freshly verified.

C12.note: stepLoop is message-driven, without hardcoded step counts.

C13.note: CLI reads root spec plus explicit --dep files only. It does not advertise automatic recursive resolution. Caller must include the full EXTENDS/INSTANCE closure. The complete send still lacks C2 bounds.

C14.note: Existing Haskell optional encoders send null or omit by message, per the documented oracle asymmetry.

C15.note: --cinit propagates constInit; caller selects a valid initializer for CONSTANTS.

C16.note: Bound is passed to registration with no local cap. Server rejects out-of-range values synchronously; this rule does not require local validation.

C17.note: IDs can cross connections, but poll/await/cancel discard returned IDs. Submission also ignores accepted kind. A foreign outcome can be associated with the requested job. Dropped reply IDs are a defensive correctness concern; these numbered clauses do not explicitly prescribe an ID-equality check, so this is not counted as an unambiguous numbered MUST breach.

C18.note: awaitJob preserves optional timeout and re-awaits nonterminal status. A terminal status without result makes one final poll, then errors.

C19.note: Explicit cancel helper accepts only JobStatus, whereas guide reply grammar also permits JobResult. Both current Haskell and Lean servers return status on cancel; no current-server failure is asserted.

C20.note: runClientValidateAsync unwraps JobValidateDone into the same ValidateResult as sync. Infrastructure errors remain errors.

C21.note: Unknown causes one extra query and then terminal error. There is no indefinite unknown retry loop expecting the job to appear.

C22.note: No automatic pool. register_error maps to Left, including a full queue. Applications own connection limits.

C23.note: No explicit completion ordering assumption, but dropping returned IDs fails to correlate independent jobs. See C17 finding. Dropped reply IDs are a defensive correctness concern; these numbered clauses do not explicitly prescribe an ID-equality check, so this is not counted as an unambiguous numbered MUST breach.

C24.note: TLS13 is the only supported version; client credentials and CA are loaded; certificate-request hook returns the credential.

C25.note: Uses defaultParamsClient host with CA. No explicit SAN-only policy hook is present. Dependency implementation is unavailable locally; CN-only rejection is not established. Wildcard differences are documented.

C26.note: Peer SHA256 pin is checked before protocol but compared as case-sensitive Text. Uppercase valid pins fail. Guide section 10 explicitly records this Haskell difference. Explicit registry pin precedence is correct.

C27.note: POSIX check forbids only group/other access (077). It accepts 0400, 0700 and special bits rather than literal 0600. Windows ACL exception is explicit.

findings.title: Empty TLS serverName disables SAN identity checks
findings.trigger: A caller passes serverName := some "" to the MirrorLean TLS API.
findings.observed: The default and wrong-name controls reject the CA-valid CN-only peer, but the empty override connects. On the SAN-bearing peer, the normal control connects and a wrong name rejects.
findings.impact: An empty configuration value can reduce authentication to CA-chain validation, accepting a peer without the intended SAN identity. This does not demonstrate a fingerprint-pin bypass.
findings.fixDirection: Reject an empty effective server name before connection and retain defensive SAN setup in the C shim.

findings.title: Comment markers inside TLA+ strings hide dependencies
findings.trigger: A valid string literal containing "(*" precedes Helper == INSTANCE Dep.
findings.observed: The control resolves two sources including Dep; the marker case reports success with only the root source and no Dep.
findings.impact: The client can send an incomplete inline EXTENDS/INSTANCE closure for a valid model, leading to downstream registration/compilation failure.
findings.fixDirection: Track quoted strings and escapes when stripping comments, then cover marker strings before INSTANCE and EXTENDS declarations.

findings.title: Callback negotiation admits an invalid target/computer pairing
findings.trigger: Select mirrorecma-v1 with mirrors.async-state-computer/v1 without an explicit execution field.
findings.observed: The invalid callback selection is accepted and invokes factory/computer/dispose once. The same pair with execution: "sync" rejects locally with state_computer_contract_mismatch and zero calls/sends.
findings.impact: One public overload reaches application construction despite an incompatible local computer-contract declaration.
findings.fixDirection: Apply the same target/computer-contract pairing admission before transport and factory acquisition across overloads.

findings.title: Optional C++ Gate integration loses structured failure families
findings.trigger: A post-match factory returns a classified Gate admission, worker-protocol or deadline error.
findings.observed: The actual public runner maps three distinct input codes with identical human text to adapter_factory_failed. Normal replay and wrong-digest zero-factory controls behave correctly.
findings.impact: The optional facade cannot recover the original stable failure family from Error or SandboxEvidence. Base wire compatibility is not disproved by this finding.
findings.fixDirection: Preserve trusted original Gate code/stage at the integration boundary while retaining primary failures and ordinary Mirrors mismatch.
findings.limit: Runtime probe uses FakeTransport and classified factory results, not a real Gate process. The actual Gate path and generated invoke/observe error loss are source-traced only.

findings.title: Built-in CLI accepts a JSON reply without its terminating LF
findings.trigger: A TCP peer sends a complete spec_validated JSON object without newline and then closes.
findings.observed: Both the valid-LF control and the missing-LF case print VALID and exit 0.
findings.impact: The CLI accepts an unterminated frame that the guide requires it to reject. All four SDKs have strict EOF/LF rejection in their source paths.
findings.fixDirection: Reject nonempty buffered bytes at EOF or read failure unless a complete LF-terminated frame was received.
findings.limit: Plain TCP was reproduced. The analogous TLS receive branch is source evidence only.

findings.title: Trace capture writes cancel_job after terminal protocol_error
findings.trigger: An accepted async trace job receives protocol_error in response to await_job.
findings.observed: The recorded exchange is register_trace_gen_async → await_job → cancel_job, with protocol_error before the final write. The CLI retains the original stderr and exits 2.
findings.impact: Cleanup sends another flow message on a connection the guide declares unusable. The original error is not overwritten.
findings.fixDirection: Separate local poll-budget cancellation from peer/protocol-terminal failures and cancel only while the connection remains usable.

findings.title: Haskell transport paths lack the 65,535-byte bound
findings.trigger: An outgoing registration/state is oversized, or a peer supplies an oversized unterminated line.
findings.observed: sendMsg encodes without a final size check; TCP/stdio line readers and TLS buffer accumulation have no uniform payload cap.
findings.impact: Oversized messages can be emitted and receive memory can grow beyond the mandated bound before JSON parsing.
findings.fixDirection: Centralize final encoded-send validation and bounded raw-byte line reads, including UTF-8 boundary controls.
findings.limit: Confirmed by current source inspection; no Haskell runtime or build was run.

contractDiscrepancies.title: Clarify async register_error: failed attempt or terminal connection?
contractDiscrepancies.text: C5 says to stop the session and use a new connection after register_error. Section 10 says it is terminal for that register attempt. The server async dispatcher and all four SDKs intentionally retain the connection after a queue-full rejection. Closing it can cancel other jobs owned by that connection under C6. Reconcile the guide/server contract before changing clients. This ambiguity does not excuse F6: protocol_error is explicitly terminal.

contractDiscrepancies.title: Clarify exact 0600 versus owner-only key permissions
contractDiscrepancies.text: Rust enforces exactly mode & 07777 == 0600. ECMA, C++, Lean, the built-in CLI and Haskell reject group/other access but accept owner-only 0400/0700 and special-bit variants. These do not match the literal rule. Owner-only modes do not by themselves demonstrate private-key exposure; decide whether to enforce the exact mode or document the intended private-only policy.

additionalObservations.title: Haskell reply identity correlation
additionalObservations.text: Public async helpers discard echoed job IDs and accepted job kind. This is a source-confirmed defensive correctness concern, but C17/C23 do not explicitly require an ID-equality check. It is not counted among the seven unambiguous implementation gaps.

additionalObservations.title: Haskell cancel response grammar
additionalObservations.text: cancelJob accepts job_status only, while the guide permits job_result too. Both current servers return job_status, so this is a source-only compatibility gap for another legal peer response, not a demonstrated current-server regression.

additionalObservations.title: MirrorLean nullable config decoder
additionalObservations.text: The convenience ApalacheConfig JSON decoder accepts an absent constInit but rejects explicit null. Normal typed outbound requests omit absent fields and remain compliant with C14. The remote closure probe also records this peripheral API difference.

additionalObservations.title: Historical Haskell TLS policy
additionalObservations.text: Case-sensitive fingerprint comparison is a documented reference exception. SAN-only validation through its TLS dependency was not established by this audit; no CN-fallback defect is asserted.

limits: Read-only audit of the inspected checkout revisions. No source fixes or commits were made.
Six focused findings were reproduced on remote Windows-dev Ubuntu WSL. All compilation and runtime probes ran remotely; no local builds/tests or model checking ran.
Source-supported cells mean implementation and/or test-source evidence, not a fresh runtime pass or a proof of universal conformance.
Full SDK suites, the full transport/interop matrix, Haskell runtime, and actual Gate backend failure injection were not rerun.
MI and SO requirements are conditional on advertised profiles. Descriptor mode is ECMA-only; Lean required verification has no prefer fallback and no Gate facade.
Caller-owned model inputs, complete manual source closures, observations, deployment policy and tool mediation remain caller/host obligations.
The per-client raw reports are the preceding static-review snapshots. This aggregate and remote evidence provide their validation update.
